thread:
lia-sales: FYI ACME POC is blocked — streaming responses over our PrivateLink keep timing out after ~30s. They see an initial chunk, then nothing. Can eng swarm?

sam-eng: Got it, can you paste the client logs + a raw curl that reproduces? Is this only over PrivateLink or also public endpoint? SDK and version?

lia-sales: Repro steps from the customer (TS SDK v0.9.2 behind corp proxy / F5):
```
# client logs
[2026-03-19T16:12:03Z] request start POST /v1/streams
[2026-03-19T16:12:04Z] got 200 headers
[2026-03-19T16:12:34Z] no new data for 30s -> client timeout
```
curl they used (via PrivateLink):
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer xxxxx" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  https://redwood-inference.internal/v1/streams/chat --http1.1
```
Notes: public endpoint works for short responses but their bigger chats hang on PrivateLink.

devex-bot: :robot_face: New POC thread recorded for ACME — tagging eng and security.

tony-arch: Two quick guesses: 1) some LB/proxy in the PrivateLink path may be buffering or dropping chunked transfer frames (F5 and ALB variants do this). 2) the corp proxy might be rewriting Connection/Transfer-Encoding headers.
Try these quick tests: reroute the same client to a public/redwood-hosted endpoint (no PrivateLink) to confirm the difference; and run curl with --no-buffer to force flush. Also check if their proxy converts streaming to chunked+Content-Length which breaks server streaming.

sam-eng: Workaround ideas while we triage: extend client-side idle timeout to 90s, enable SDK polling fallback, and disable proxy buffering if possible. Example config snippets:

TypeScript SDK (ts-sdk v0.9+):
```
const client = new RedwoodClient({
  baseURL: process.env.REDWOOD_PUBLIC_URL || "https://api.redwood.com",
  timeout: 90000, // 90s
  streaming: true,
  proxy: {
    // if corp proxy does chunk coalescing, try bypass for POC
    hostname: 'squid.corp.local',
    port: 3128,
    keepAlive: true
  }
});
```
Python (requests) fallback to longer read timeout:
```
s = requests.Session()
s.get(url, stream=True, timeout=(5, 120))
```
If they can hit the public endpoint and streaming works, that's a clear PrivateLink/proxy path issue.

sam-eng: Also please capture the raw headers we send back (especially: Transfer-Encoding, Content-Type, Connection). If their proxy strips or replaces Transfer-Encoding: chunked, streaming will stall.

lia-sales: Quick question on pricing for ACME — if we keep them on hosted while we triage PrivateLink, will POC usage be billed normally or covered by the pilot credits? They want to know cost implications if we ask them to test public endpoint.

ryan-support: For POCs we generally apply pilot credits to hosted usage if sales approves it. Public endpoint traffic would count against hosted usage but we can apply credits for the trial window (I can coordinate approvals today). Dedicated/Private deployments require separate contract/commit and are not covered by pilot credits.

sara-sec: Security note: PrivateLink requires us to publish the set of ENI IPs and service name for their VPC policy. Also they may need to whitelist our internal ALB health checks. I'll DM the standard IP list and the questionnaire snippet to lia-sales. For PII workloads we recommend a Dedicated/Private setup (customer asked about SOC2 controls).

tony-arch: If rerouting for a quick test is fine, try: 1) direct client -> public endpoint (no PrivateLink), 2) curl --no-buffer to the same host, 3) capture tcpdump on client side to see whether chunks are arriving but not forwarded. If chunks arrive and client doesn't get them, it's the corp proxy. If chunks never arrive, it's PrivateLink path/LB.

lia-sales: Thanks — I'm going to ask ACME to run the public endpoint test and try the timeout bump. I'll post results here. Also looping in legal for the ENI whitelist.

sam-eng: Ping me the curl output and headers. If it's the F5 behavior we can propose a short-term workaround (switch to event-batching mode or use non-streaming API for the POC).

ryan-support: I'll queue the credits approval once lia-sales confirms the test route.

lia-sales: Will do, thx everyone :pray:
